summary: Preserved the candidate's fd-aware bounded LRU and socket lifecycle fixes, but replaced its active-sender cache overflow with condition-variable backpressure. Also added a bounded retry for real libzmq asynchronous fd retirement. Under RLIMIT_NOFILE=128, the exact candidate failed after 38 locked endpoints; the corrected real-PyZMQ regression holds the cache at its derived bound and completes after a sender releases.

tests.what_was_measured: The exact candidate derived cache_size=21, completed and locked 38 distinct endpoints, overflowed the cache to 38, and real PyZMQ raised ZMQError: Too many open files during socket/monitor creation.

Seven candidate tests passed and its real low-RLIMIT sequential test failed at get_monitor_socket with Too many open files on the prepared host, independently exposing transient libzmq fd retirement during rapid churn.
Nine corrected tests passed, including real-PyZMQ sequential churn and active-endpoint backpressure under soft RLIMIT_NOFILE=128.
380 tests and 47 subtests passed across the broader disaggregation and environment suites.
All applicable formatting, lint, syntax, spelling, registry, and repository policy hooks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: The reproduced defect and correction are in host-side CommonKVManager/PyZMQ descriptor management; no GPU kernel participates. The unavailable 16x H800 distributed workload was not represented by a smaller fixture.

remaining_limitations: The reporter's 16x NVIDIA H800 full-model, multi-node workload and weights were unavailable; validation covers the actual host-side manager and real PyZMQ path only.
No GPU execution was needed for this descriptor lifecycle, and no native source changed.
An explicitly oversized SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ZMQ_SOCKET_CACHE_SIZE remains capable of exceeding the descriptor budget because explicit configuration intentionally overrides the derived default.
